title: The 20 Percent Proposal That Vanished in One Day: The Oil Market’s Next Turn
part1:
Think of the oil market as a suspense story lasting only two days. On the first day, a major fee proposal appears, and on the next day, it is suddenly withdrawn. Yet the story does not end there. Prices fell back once, then quickly returned to a higher level.

The first act was July 13. Trump posted that he would seek a 20 percent reimbursement from all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz, to cover the cost of ensuring security that the United States was paying.

However, this was not an actual fee system that had started. The rate was the only thing proposed. Who would pay, what it would be based on, and how it would be collected were not explained. A large number had appeared on the stage before anything else.
part2:
On that day, Brent crude futures ended at $83.30 a barrel. They rose $7.29 from the day before, a gain of 9.59 percent. Reuters linked this rise to a US naval blockade of Iran that was expected to begin the next day, and to concerns about energy shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

The second act came the next day, July 14. Trump posted that the 20 percent reimbursement fee would be replaced with deals involving Gulf countries’ trade with the United States or their investments there. The fee proposal announced the day before had changed into a different proposal in just one day.
part3:
You might have thought prices would keep falling, but the market had one more twist. After the withdrawal was announced, Brent briefly gave up some of its gains. But before long, it returned to a high level close to where it had been before the announcement. At the time of the report, it was about 2.6 percent higher than the previous day and above $85 a barrel. Trading on the 14th also ended at $84.73 a barrel, higher than the day before.

The key point in this news is that, even though the fee proposal disappeared, the concerns surrounding the strait did not. The naval blockade, attacks between the United States and Iran, and concerns about tanker safety continued. Even when the policy shown on the screen changed, the risks at sea remained. The oil market’s two days became a short suspense story in which these two stories moved at the same time.
in_one_line: The proposed 20 percent Hormuz fee vanished in a day, but lingering shipping risks kept oil prices high.
